assumptions: Authorized users can obtain sufficiently granular passport and battery-management data for each transaction.
A reliable battery identity can bind those records and any bench test to the physical asset.
A transaction platform will accept an independent probabilistic score in a material decision.
Post-transaction outcomes can be retained lawfully to calibrate the model.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed paid integration plus a blinded validation set showing incremental prediction accuracy, reduced pricing or routing loss, fraud resistance, certificate acceptance, repeat transaction volume, contribution margin, and insurable liability.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A transaction-specific certificate that reconciles passport, operating, event, and physical-test evidence addresses the real gap between raw health fields and a price, credit, or routing decision.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Battery mispricing and misrouting can be material, but no marketplace, lessor, financier, insurer, or repurposer has specified acceptance criteria or committed budget for the certificate.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Per-certificate and API revenue is legible, but partner integration, authenticated data access, dispute review, liability, and optional physical testing make both volume thresholds and margins highly uncertain.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Secondary battery decisions should grow, yet the initial customer spans auctions, fleets, finance, insurance, repurposing, and recycling without a validated first workflow or transaction volume.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: OEMs, battery analytics firms, test-equipment vendors, and transaction platforms possess better data or workflow control and can expose or bundle competing scores.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: If independently trusted, the same certificate could serve resale, lease return, underwriting, repurposing, recycling, and multiple battery categories across borders.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Outcome calibration could become proprietary, but the feedback loop, identity chain, underlying records, and platform access are not owned and may be withheld.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder fits the modeling problem but has no battery dataset, accredited test capability, OEM interface, transaction channel, or institutional trust for a consequential score.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Battery-passport rollout and statutory access to health parameters create timely data availability as secondary battery transactions become more important.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Embedding at a marketplace, lessor, or financier is the right route, but each route requires an unproven enterprise integration and the accepting platform retains the customer relationship.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Heterogeneous telemetry, battery identity, tampering, physical testing, model validation, safety liability, and long enterprise cycles make a trusted certificate difficult within the stated capital and time limits.

highest_value_structural_change: Begin with one lessor or auction workflow that contractually supplies identity-bound records, uses a partner-delivered standardized test, and makes the certificate an explicit pricing or routing input with outcome feedback rights.
main_structural_strength: The paid event is attached to a specific high-value battery transaction, and subsequent outcomes could create a useful calibration loop rather than a generic analytics report.
primary_score_limiter: The venture controls neither the authenticated input data nor the workflow acceptance that would make its score trusted and economically consequential.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Entitled actors may receive core state-of-health data directly, while OEM models or a standardized physical capacity test may outperform and commoditize an independent cross-brand statistical certificate.
